_doc: THE ONE PIN of the gh binary libs:gh ships (#646). build.gradle reads this file, downloads each ABI's official release tarball ONCE into build/, refuses on a sha256 mismatch of the tarball AND of the extracted binary (the #288 / #348 fetch-once-refuse-on-mismatch pattern, as libs:rclone does it), reads the ELF program headers and refuses if PT_INTERP is present, and lands the binary as jniLibs/<abi>/libgh.so. That name is not decoration: on API 29+ an app may not exec a file it wrote into its own data directory (W^X), but it MAY exec what the installer extracted into nativeLibraryDir, and only files named lib*.so get extracted there — which is also why the PACKAGING app must set packaging.jniLibs.useLegacyPackaging = true (AGP's default keeps .so files compressed inside the APK and mmaps them, extracting nothing). GhRunner execs applicationInfo.nativeLibraryDir + '/libgh.so'.
_doc_interp: WHY THE OFFICIAL linux_{arch} BUILD RUNS ON ANDROID. gh's release binaries for linux_arm64 and linux_amd64 are Go builds with cgo disabled: measured 2026-09-29 on the real device (a0_docs/eng-specs/terminal-per-tool-libs-measurement.md §7b) and RE-MEASURED 2026-09-29 for this pin with an independent program-header walk over both binaries — NO PT_INTERP and NO PT_DYNAMIC, i.e. fully static, raw syscalls, no libc at all. Bionic vs glibc is therefore moot: nothing is dynamically linked, so the kernel runs it directly. That is the property `interp: none` below declares and build.gradle re-measures on every build; a future release that links dynamically fails the build here rather than dying ENOENT on a phone. DO NOT SUBSTITUTE THE NIXPKGS gh: the gh in this phone's nix store is a DIFFERENT artifact, 49,750,856 bytes with BOTH PT_INTERP and PT_DYNAMIC present, and it would be refused by the guard below. The official cli/cli release is the one pinned here; do not generalise from a distro build.
_doc_size: 37.1 MB (arm64) / 40.0 MB (amd64) uncompressed — CHEAPER than the 78 MB rclone binary this shelf already ships. ~13-15 MB in the APK (the release tarball's own compression is the floor) and extracted once at install. A per-ABI split APK carries one of them.
_doc_selfcontained: ZERO CHILD EXECS, NO git, NO PATH, NO WRITABLE $HOME — all measured, including a real authenticated API round-trip (`gh api /user`) whose strace showed only gh's own execve and nothing else. gh shells out to git only for git-shaped subcommands, which the auth and REST paths this library uses never reach. GH_CONFIG_DIR overrides config AND state location completely, so the consuming app points it at its own filesDir and gh needs nothing from $HOME. That is what makes gh safe to exec from nativeLibraryDir in an Android sandbox.
_doc_device_flow: WHY THIS LIBRARY EXISTS AT ALL (#646 rung 2). The official static gh carries GitHub's OWN GitHub App client ids, and BOTH were exercised live against GitHub's device-code endpoint on 2026-09-29: Iv1.b231c327f1eaa229 returned user_code F7FD-4222 and Iv1.e7b89e013f801f03 returned C503-AFF0, both with verification_uri https://github.com/login/device. So the device flow is ENABLED on GitHub's side for gh's app: there is NOTHING to register, no client secret to mint and no provider setting for the owner to toggle. This is the exact opposite of the dead end #629/#641 hit, where OUR OWN declared client was a GitHub APP (Ov23li… prefix) and GitHub Apps ship Device Flow OFF — that provider was deleted rather than documented, and it stays deleted: this library does not re-declare it in auth.sign_in.providers. It authenticates through GITHUB'S app, not ours. The `client_ids` below are the ids MEASURED inside the pinned binary; they are recorded so a future release that rotates them is caught by the tester rather than discovered on a phone.
